title: Penne alla Vodka
subtitle: Tomato, cream, and vodka pasta sauce
excerpt: A rich, pink pasta sauce made from a tomato base finished with cream and a measure of vodka. The vodka releases fat-soluble flavour compounds from the tomato that water and oil alone cannot, adding depth without any alcohol taste.

recipe.sourceNotes: Penne alla vodka appeared in the Italian restaurant scene in the late 1970s and 1980s. Its precise origin is disputed: different stories credit Roman restaurants, Neapolitan chefs, and Italian-American restaurants in New York. The alcohol in the vodka evaporates during cooking; its role is to act as a solvent for tomato flavour compounds that are not water-soluble, resulting in a deeper, more complex tomato taste.

content.text: Add the vodka after the tomatoes and let it cook for 3 to 4 minutes so the alcohol evaporates before you add the cream. The cream goes in at the end and barely needs to cook; just stir it through and let the sauce warm gently. Overcooking cream in an acidic tomato sauce can cause it to split.
Cook the penne in heavily salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 100 ml pasta water before draining.

Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the shallots and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, season with salt, and cook for 5 minutes, breaking up the tomatoes.
Add the vodka, stir, and simmer for 4 minutes until most of the alcohol has cooked off. Reduce the heat to low and stir in the cream. Simmer gently for 3 minutes. Add the parmesan and stir to melt.
Toss the drained penne in the sauce with a splash of pasta water. Scatter with parsley and extra parmesan. Serve immediately.
